title: Fun with Strings
story: You're making a custom birthday card for your best friend. Instead of writing the same message for everyone, you want the computer to mix and match greetings, names, and messages to create something personal!
why: Building strings from pieces lets programs create personalized messages, reports, and displays for every user.
analogy: String concatenation is like building a LEGO tower — you snap pieces together one at a time until you have something big.
try_it: Build a sentence about yourself from 3 variables! Create variables for your name, a verb (like "loves"), and a thing (like "dogs"), then concatenate them into a story.
tips: Always include spaces in your strings where needed — concat doesn't add them automatically!
You can nest concat calls to join more than two strings at once
String variables always need the type `Str` and values go in double quotes
common_mistakes: Forgetting spaces between words — `"Hello" + "World"` becomes `"HelloWorld"`, not `"Hello World"`
Using `+` to join strings in XIOM — you must use `string.str_concat()`, not the plus sign
